proposal.name: Complete trained two-head residual drafting
proposal.idea: Train and activate the unresolved round-0026 predictor: use an already-computed target feature and its known pending token to propose two future tokens simultaneously. Preserve suffix drafts containing at least two tokens; otherwise verify the learned proposals through the existing exact verifier.
proposal.cost_removed: With both proposals accepted, one three-position verification can replace three scalar forwards. The eligible path uses 222 target projection invocations instead of 633, plus two auxiliary projections. Target arithmetic remains, but scheduling and repeated weight reads can be amortized. The predictor adds 2,656,512 BF16 parameter bytes, one two-row vocabulary projection, and no auxiliary transformer or KV computation.
proposal.source_evidence: candidate/inference.py:121 limits suffix drafts by observed context, while :313 requires at least three positions for bulk verification. At :537 the verifier computes normalized features but returns only predictions; :621 similarly discards scalar features. Its grouped body performs seven projections across 30 layers, followed by twelve vocabulary panels. The tied [49152,576] BF16 head occupies 56,623,104 bytes, making auxiliary head cost material. experiments/0026/report.json explicitly reports that no trained artifact was produced; its patch's load_predictor returns None when both artifact files are absent. [Medusa-1](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.10774v3) supports frozen-backbone residual predictors and independent self-distillation, although it does not establish acceptance for this smaller shared-head design.
proposal.generalization: Shallow learned drafting can amortize large decoder traversals without running another transformer. Additional learned storage scales as O(hidden_size²). Ordinary dense operations and unchanged target verification make the mechanism independent of hardware, custom kernels, and compilation.
proposal.risk: The shared frozen vocabulary head and independent horizons may give poor joint acceptance. Its extra vocabulary scan, feature handling, and rejected verification work may outweigh savings. CPU-generated training features can differ numerically from native BF16 features, affecting proposal quality but never authorizing incorrect emission.
proposal.history_relation: Round 0026's 1.000x result measured an artifact-free fallback and leaves trained acceptance and throughput unresolved. Reuse its implementation as a starting point, with a CPU-capable offline artifact build and mandatory readiness checks. Round 0025 actually tested full-depth quantized drafting; this avoids those sequential auxiliary layers. Round 0027's invocation reduction failed the threshold, favoring a test that could amortize complete target traversals.

research.plan:
1. Implement only inside candidate/. Restore and audit the relevant round-0026 feature capture, predictor, and verification integration against the current baseline. Preserve all accepted verifier optimizations and the scalar pipeline.

2. Complete training before handoff. Provide an offline CPU-capable trainer using an independent FP32 copy of the pinned target's unchanged weight values and tokenizer; auxiliary training need not reproduce reference arithmetic. Freeze this trainer before evaluation. Use Salesforce/wikitext, wikitext-2-raw-v1, train split at revision b08601e04326c79dfdd32d625aee71d232d685c3. Join rows with newlines, tokenize without added special tokens, and select 4096 nonoverlapping 128-token blocks with NumPy default_rng(0). Generate 64 greedy continuation tokens per block, continuing after EOS. Use no harness prompts, outputs, timings, or request-time training.

3. For each continuation, pair feature f_i that produced token y_i with embedding(y_i), and label the following two tokens, for i=0..61. Train only A[1152,1152] and b[1152]: reshape A·concat(f_i,embedding(y_i))+b into two rows, apply SiLU, add f_i, and project through the frozen vocabulary matrix. Retain the prior recipe: zero initialization, FP32 training, three epochs, batch size 256, equal cross-entropy losses, seeded shuffling, and AdamW with learning rate 1e-3, betas (0.9,0.999), epsilon 1e-8, and weight decay 0.01. Export BF16 parameters and a manifest containing provenance, hashes, backend, and 2976 completed updates. Missing or invalid artifacts must stop supported-target evaluation clearly; an untrained or disabled predictor is not a completed experiment.

4. Capture existing normalized target features without recomputation or changed target forward shapes. Prefill may retain its final prompt feature and load immutable auxiliary parameters, but must not run the predictor. Pair each scalar pending output with its feature and processed-prefix offset. After suffix verification, retain the feature corresponding to the selected corrective or bonus prediction.

5. At an existing drained boundary, preserve ordinary suffix drafts of length at least two. Otherwise require aligned features, actual grouped-verifier eligibility, three remaining output slots, and KV capacity through C+3. Produce two proposal tensors and verify [pending,d0,d1]. Materialize proposals and target predictions together. For acceptance length a, emit drafts[:a] followed by prediction p_a, trim 2-a entries, and retain target feature f_a tagged C+a+1. Charge all generated-token-dependent work to decode; keep request state isolated.

6. Require native checks using the actual trained artifact, including positive predictor-call counts on independent fixtures, every acceptance length, feature alignment, suffix/scalar transitions, capacity boundaries, small budgets, unchanged target parameters, and retained-KV parity. Then have the orchestrator run exact-token evaluation and both throughput confirmations against the current best. Keep only the required improvement; do not retrain or tune policy from benchmark results. If artifact production cannot finish, record an implementation limitation without timing the fallback as this experiment.
research.reason: Active learned drafting remains untested. Completing its artifact provides a sound experiment with substantial potential amortization and a cheaper auxiliary path than the tested full-depth drafter; exactness and net throughput remain evaluation questions.

proposal.name: Complete trained two-head residual drafting
proposal.idea: Complete and activate round 0026’s unresolved predictor. Use an already-computed normalized target feature and its known pending token to propose two future tokens simultaneously. Preserve suffix drafts containing at least two tokens; otherwise verify eligible learned proposals through the existing exact target verifier.
proposal.cost_removed: When both proposals match, one three-position verification emits three new tokens using 222 target projection calls instead of 633 across three scalar forwards, plus two auxiliary projection calls. Target arithmetic for verified positions remains; scheduling and repeated weight access can be amortized. The predictor adds 2,656,512 BF16 parameter bytes, an embedding lookup, a two-row vocabulary projection, feature retention, and rejected-position work. The shared vocabulary matrix occupies 56,623,104 bytes. The scalar comparison is illustrative because the current baseline also supports one-token suffix drafts.
proposal.source_evidence: Verified [candidate/inference.py](candidate/inference.py:313): bulk verification requires at least three positions, and the existing scalar and verifier paths already compute the required normalized features. Installed mlx-lm 0.32.0 exposes the same body-then-head decomposition. The pinned checkpoint confirms 30 layers and a tied BF16 [49152,576] vocabulary matrix. [harness/bench.py](harness/bench.py:20) synchronizes around decode and shares the target model between implementations. The [round-0026 report](experiments/0026/report.json) confirms that training produced no artifact; its patch returns no predictor when both artifact files are absent. [Medusa-1](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.10774v3) supports frozen-backbone residual predictors and self-distillation, but trains separate vocabulary heads and does not establish this shared-head design’s acceptance.
proposal.generalization: For a fixed number of horizons, auxiliary parameter storage scales as O(hidden_size²), without another transformer or auxiliary KV cache. Shallow proposals and exact verification can amortize decoder execution using ordinary dense operations across hardware and runtimes. Vocabulary projection work remains O(vocabulary_size × hidden_size); physical weight reuse and speedup require measurement.
proposal.risk: Independent horizons and the frozen shared vocabulary head may give poor joint acceptance. FP32 teacher features and continuations can differ from native BF16 execution, further reducing proposal quality. Extra vocabulary work, feature handling, limited drained-boundary opportunities, and rejected verification may outweigh savings. Feature capture and rollback must preserve target arithmetic, cache contents, and bounded request-local lifetimes.
proposal.history_relation: Round 0026’s approximately 1.000x result measured an artifact-free fallback, leaving active learned drafting unresolved. Reuse its integration after auditing it against the current baseline. Round 0025 actually tested sequential full-depth quantized drafting; this predictor avoids those auxiliary transformer passes. Round 0027 shows that fewer projection calls alone do not establish a throughput gain.

review.plan:
1. Implement only inside candidate/. Keep auxiliary parameters and training separate from target modules. Preserve all accepted verifier optimizations, suffix drafting, and scalar pipeline scheduling. For feature f and pending-token embedding e, compute u=concat(f,e)@A.T+b, with A=[1152,1152] and b=[1152]. Reshape u into two 576-element rows, form q_j=f+SiLU(u_j), and project both rows together through the unchanged tied vocabulary matrix. Their argmax IDs are proposals only; add no normalization or approximate acceptance rule.

2. Provide a genuinely CPU-capable offline trainer whose import path does not import MLX, candidate.inference, or initialize an accelerator. Load an independent FP32 copy of the exact BF16 weight values, configuration, and tokenizer from mlx-community/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct revision 422de227b90002f443a21a58b1087f6ee7632731. Verify complete tensor loading and tied-head mapping; freeze every target parameter. Auxiliary training need not reproduce native arithmetic. Batch independent training prompts and bound feature storage as needed, recording execution settings before evaluation. Keep training dependencies and temporary files within candidate/.

3. Freeze the corpus and recipe before evaluation. Use [Salesforce/wikitext at the pinned revision](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Salesforce/wikitext/tree/b08601e04326c79dfdd32d625aee71d232d685c3/wikitext-2-raw-v1), configuration wikitext-2-raw-v1, train split. Join rows in dataset order with newlines, tokenize without added special tokens, partition into nonoverlapping 128-token blocks, and select 4096 blocks without replacement using NumPy default_rng(0). Generate exactly 64 greedy continuation tokens per block, continuing after EOS, with fresh sequence state. Use no harness prompts, outputs, timings, or request-time training.

4. Let f_i be the normalized teacher feature that produced continuation token y_i. Train on (f_i, embedding(y_i)) with labels (y_(i+1), y_(i+2)) for i=0..61, without crossing continuation boundaries: 253,952 examples. Initialize A and b to zero. Optimize only these parameters in FP32 for three epochs, batch size 256, using the mean cross-entropy across both horizons. Use a separate default_rng(0) shuffle generator, AdamW learning rate 1e-3, betas (0.9,0.999), epsilon 1e-8, weight decay 0.01, and bias correction. Keep the frozen vocabulary projection differentiable with respect to residual rows. Complete 992 updates per epoch, 2976 total; export the final A and b to BF16 without benchmark-based checkpoint selection.

5. Finish artifact production before handoff. Deliver parameters and a manifest containing the recipe, completed updates, selected spans, corpus/feature/continuation hashes, target/tokenizer hashes, trainer source hash, backend, versions, and artifact hash. Validate expected keys, shapes, BF16 dtype, finite values, and evidence that training changed the zero initialization. On the supported target, missing, incomplete, or invalid artifacts must raise clearly before authoritative evaluation, including when request eligibility would otherwise skip drafting. Load and materialize immutable parameters during prefill or earlier preparation. If training cannot finish, report an implementation limitation; do not benchmark a disabled or untrained fallback as this experiment.

6. Capture existing normalized features without recomputation or changed target forward shapes. Preserve the full prompt-shaped head during prefill and the singleton scalar head during decode. Prefill may retain its final prompt feature, but must not embed the generated pending token or run the predictor. Expose already-computed normalized rows from every verifier branch. Carry each scalar output’s feature and processed-prefix offset alongside its token in the existing bounded pending queue, preserving submit-successor-before-host-read ordering and the existing draining rule. Copy only retained rows where necessary to release larger buffers.

7. Draft only at an existing drained boundary. With history H and common KV offset C, require len(H)=C+1: KV represents H[:C], pending is H[C], and its target feature is tagged C. Obtain the unchanged suffix draft first; preserve it when its length is at least two. Otherwise require valid feature metadata, at least three remaining output slots, capacity through C+3 in every key and value buffer, and the verifier’s actual batched/grouped eligibility, including cached false decisions. Keep rotary, attention, and vocabulary-panel fallbacks independent. Failed request eligibility preserves existing behavior, including one-token suffix drafts. Construct both proposal tensors and verify [pending,d0,d1] without intermediate host token reads or auxiliary KV writes.

8. Materialize both proposal IDs and all three target predictions together at the verification completion boundary. For consecutive matching-prefix length a in 0..2, commit drafts[:a] followed by target prediction p_a. Retain p_a with the target normalized feature from verifier row a, trim exactly 2-a KV positions after verification completes, and tag the retained feature C+a+1. Apply the same selected-row rule to suffix blocks. Never retain the final rejected row or an auxiliary residual as the target feature. Charge all generated-token-dependent embedding, prediction, feature handling, verification, transfers, bookkeeping, and cleanup to decode. Only immutable parameters may persist across requests; clear request features and obsolete references in finally cleanup.

9. Require native differential checks with the actual trained artifact. Check captured prompt/scalar/verifier features, target logits, emitted tokens, retained KV, unchanged target parameter values and identities, and reference execution on the shared model. Exercise real learned proposals with positive predictor-call counts, plus separately controlled acceptance lengths 0, 1, and 2; consecutive blocks; suffix/scalar transitions; small budgets; capacity growth and unequal K/V capacities; cached eligibility failures; and fresh requests. Keep legacy fixtures explicitly isolated from auxiliary activation, and exclude test overrides from authoritative evaluation. Check missing and invalid artifacts fail clearly.

10. Freeze the artifact and policy before authoritative evaluation. Have the orchestrator run exact-token evaluation and both throughput confirmations against the current best under the existing synchronized timing boundary. Record predictor calls, proposed tokens, accepted auxiliary proposals excluding bonus tokens, and whether the scored path activated. Keep only exact output with at least 1.03x gain in both confirmations. Do not retrain or tune from benchmark results.
review.reason: No fundamental flaw was found. In-memory execution of the restored round-0026 control flow with a deterministic NumPy target stand-in and installed KVCache logic passed 1,050 decode simulations, 5,018 feature-alignment checks, and 2,250 eligibility cases. These establish bookkeeping only. The review strengthens CPU-training independence, artifact readiness, cost accounting, and native active-path validation; trained acceptance and throughput remain experimental. No files were edited.

implementation.summary: Integrated two-head residual drafting, feature retention, exact verification, strict artifact loading, and native differential checks. Completed all 2,976 CPU training updates and delivered the validated BF16 artifact and provenance manifest. Only candidate/ changed. Native checks require the supported target because this sandbox cannot initialize Metal; authoritative evaluation and benchmarking remain with the orchestrator.
